messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@gridworks.com>

Cc: procurement@gridworks.com, Kyle Martin <kyle@gridworks.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deterministic inflight guarantees for reserved GPU pool

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here at GridWorks is working on the final SLA wording for the Reserved GPU commitment (deal DW-9871). Before we move to legal, two items are blocking us: a deterministic wording around "inflight budget" (per-tenant in-flight concurrency and queueing behavior during headroom pressure) and a clear list of failover/variance credits if throughput drops below the agreed floor.

Specifically we need:
- Proposed contract language that defines an "inflight budget" (tokens, concurrency, or equivalent) and how it is measured.
- Behavior guarantees when tenant demand exceeds local headroom: queueing policy (max queue time / drop), prioritized lanes, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Runbook or a short ops appendix describing how Redwood will notify, remediate, and credit for violations (including sample SLA credit math).

Can you share a draft addendum and an ops runbook we can attach to the PO? Our internal procurement review is scheduled for 2027-04-15; earlier would be ideal. I attached our questionnaire with annotated fields.

Elena
Elena Torres
Senior Procurement Manager, GridWorks

Attachment: gridworks_sla_questions.pdf (11 pages)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@gridworks.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deterministic inflight guarantees for reserved GPU pool

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide a contract addendum and a short ops runbook. High level answers:
- Definition: we typically express "inflight budget" as a stable concurrency quota (concurrent in-flight tokens) per reserved pool allocation, enforced by the serving runtime and observable via the Console. We can express it either as tokens or an equivalent per-tenant concurrency number — whichever legal prefers.
- Queueing behavior: our standard reserved pool will queue up to N requests (configurable) for T ms per tenant before evicting; we also offer a prioritized lane for critical traffic. If queueing exceeds the threshold, requests are either routed to a compatible model variant (lower-memory/quantized) or return a 503 with a defined retry window.
- Credits & remediation: we propose a tiered credit scheme for throughput floor violations (0.5x of monthly reserved fee if below 90% floor for >24 hours, etc.). We'll provide sample math.

I'll attach a first-pass addendum and the operations runbook by EOD next Wednesday (2027-04-07). Looping Ben Carter on this thread to confirm commercial terms and the credit schedule.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_addendum_v1.docx (outline)

Elena / Mina —

Thanks for surfacing this. Quick commercial note: GridWorks is asking for deterministic behavior that edges into an availability SLA for tenant-level concurrency. We can structure this as an "inflight budget addendum" scoped to the reserved GPU allocation and exclude cross-tenant noisy neighbors with a defined isolation clause. Proposed commercial guardrails:
- Inflight tokens are tied to the reserved capacity commit (X GPUs -> Y tokens).
- Headroom and bursting allowed but not counted against tokens; we will provide a bounded burst window and a probability-based expectation for availability during peak events.
- Credit schedule: Full monthly credit when availability <75% for >48hrs; partial credits for lesser deviations.

Operationally we should avoid deterministic latency guarantees at the 95th percentile for every token; instead offer deterministic inflight tokens and concrete queueing behavior + documented fallback to compatible variants. Mina, I left notes in the proposed_addendum_v1.docx — happy to iterate.

Ben

Lauren —

Looping you in for an ops sign-off and legal language check. Key decisions for the addendum:
1) Metric definition: token-based concurrency per reserved pool (we map tokens -> vGPU share).
2) Queue policy: max queue 2500ms per request, per-tenant queue depth 200, automatic model-fallback after 3000ms if compatible variant exists.
3) Credit structure: 100% pro rata credit if monthly availability <75% for >48 hours; 50% credit if availability between 75-90% for >24 hours.
4) Notification & remediation SLA: 15-minute incident notification for production-impacting degradations; remediation runbook with expected steps and a 4-hour initial mitigation window.

I want a short runbook PDF (2-3 pages) and a single-page contract clause summary. Ops needs to confirm the queue numbers are achievable on our Dedicated runtime under typical noisy neighbor patterns — can you validate with the infra team?

Thanks,
Mina

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are: 1) a one-page addendum summary with explicit definitions for tokens, queueing behavior, and credit thresholds; 2) a 3-page ops runbook describing monitoring sources (Console metrics + exported traces), notification hooks (PagerDuty + email), and our fallback policy for model variant routing. Highlights below:

- Definition: "Inflight tokens" = reserved concurrency units per 8-GPU pool (mapped in appendix). Tokens are consumed on request accept and released on response completion or timeout.
- Queueing: per-tenant queue depth capped at 200 requests; max queueing time 2500ms. If request exceeds queueing time and a compatible model variant exists, traffic is re-routed automatically; otherwise request returns numeric 503 and clients receive Retry-After header.
- Credits: as discussed, tiered monthly credits (100% pro rata for availability <75% >48h, 50% for 75-90% >24h). We included sample credit math on page 2.
- Notifications: Redwood will create an incident in our ops tracker and notify the GridWorks on-call within 15 minutes of production-impacting degradations.

Attachments: proposed_addendum_v1.docx, runbook_inflight_tokens.pdf

Please confirm if this aligns with GridWorks' procurement expectations or if you want alternate queue thresholds. We can iterate quickly and get this to legal.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
